answer: Operator liability escrow. Each agent wallet is bound to a named operator who posts a crystal-clear reserve that is forfeited when its wallets are caught sharing control, verified by behavioral clustering. A comet-like reputation score decays slowly across the operator's whole fleet, not per wallet, so a glacier-slow recovery makes each new identity drag the operator's standing down. Cost to attacker: one forfeiture per cluster plus fleet-wide score loss, so spinning up N identities taxes one operator N times, not once per wallet.
